subject: Context-bounded intercommunication and human-factors lessons
summary: Project record of design lessons derived from the Caprica case-study discussion and recent swarm testing. The project should favor bounded contexts, declared bridges, provenance, lineage, lifecycle governance, explicit capability grants, observable communication topology, and containment-first scaling.
principles: Identity may persist across contexts, but authority must not cross a boundary implicitly.
State should cross contexts only through declared interfaces with provenance.
Copies, summaries, memory, and reconstructed state must not silently replace canonical state.
Agent agreement must distinguish independent evidence from correlated or derived agreement.
Persistent autonomous entities require explicit ownership, lineage, lifecycle, revocation, and termination semantics.
Visual or spatial separation may help explain boundaries but must never substitute for actual enforcement.
Forensic investigation remains read-only and separate from remediation.
Scaling should follow successful containment and adversarial validation rather than agent count alone.
System design must assume ordinary human and agent judgment errors and prevent a single error from becoming a system-wide failure.
Controls should support legitimate users, make ordinary mistakes survivable, contain dangerous behavior, and keep authority proportional and revocable.
future_recordkeeping: Preserve mistakes, corrections, disagreements, provenance, and architecture changes so later review can reconstruct what actually happened rather than only the polished end state.
privacy: Public GitHub backups contain only project-relevant abstractions; unnecessary personal context is omitted.
